title: Professional Development, Supervisor Roles, and Functions: Role of the School Counselling Internship
abstract: School counselling internships are widely regarded as a key component of counsellor training and professional development. However, research has focussed primarily on supervisees’ experiences, leaving supervisors’ roles and functions in school-based internship settings comparatively underexplored. This study employed a qualitative research design using reflexive thematic analysis to examine how school counselling internships contribute to supervisees’ professional development and to identify the roles and functions of both site-based school counsellor supervisors and academic supervisors. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with eight site-based school counsellor supervisors and four academic supervisors. Data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis, through which codes were generated from the data and organised into themes. For site-based school counsellors, the impact of internship practices on supervisees’ professional development was structured around three themes: progression in emotional experiences, personal factors, and attainments. The site-based school counsellors frequently adopted coordinator, adviser, teacher, and mentor roles in supervision; they also performed functions such as monitoring-evaluating, modelling, giving suggestions, and supporting. Academic supervisors perceived internship practices on supervisees’ professional development yielded two sub-themes: professional identity and self-awareness, and counselling skills. Academic supervisors were found to adopt the roles of coordinator, adviser, and teacher, and to perform functions such as modelling, supporting, monitoring-evaluating, informing, and providing suggestions.

journal.name: Journal of Psychologists and Counsellors in Schools
